title: Canonical module scalar tensor data and finite reduction squares
statement: Fix a finite-field datum $p,a,k=\overline{\mathbf F}_{p^a}$ and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ as in [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Use its recorded point fibre functors, the finite-Tor subcategories of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], and the finite, completed integral, rational, and common-stage derived tensors of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. For any homomorphism $f:R\to S$ of commutative rings and an ordinary-module derived scalar functor $H:D(R)\to D(S)$, scalar tensor data consist of a universal left-derived counit to termwise extension of scalars, a strong monoidal structure on $H$, and its representative tensor square with the balanced chain isomorphism $a\otimes(x\otimes y)\mapsto(a\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$. For point comparison data of [def-sf-point-fibre-tensor-system] at positive levels $m+1\ge n+1$, define finite reduction compatibility using these target scalar data for $A_{E,m+1}\to A_{E,n+1}$ and a fibre/reduction comparison whose K-flat representative is $x\mapsto1\otimes x$. The two paths from the reduced tensor fibre to the tensor of the reduced fibres must agree, using the recorded quotient tensor comparison (the comparison whose reduced-evaluation transpose defines finiteIntrinsicReductionHom), the level-$m$ and level-$n$ fibre tensorators, the fibre/reduction comparison, and the target derived scalar tensorator. Identity quotients are included. The target derived quotient functor is the ordinary-module fixed-second-factor derived tensor of [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] with the new coefficient ring in degree zero.
